is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluated Anopheles coluzzii and Anopheles gambiae collected from Yaoundé, Cameroon (Page 3, 'Methods').

reports_target_markers.evidence: Screened for Vgsc L1014F (Vgsc L995F) and L1014S (Vgsc L995S) using Real-Time PCR TaqMan assays (Page 4, 'Detection of knockdown resistance (kdr)').

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 3 on Page 8 reports extractable genotype counts for field-collected F0 mosquitoes (N=119: RR=24, RS=90, SS=5, f(R)=0.58) and F12 generation (N=111: RR=111, RS=0, SS=0, f(R)=1.0).

african_field_population.evidence: Anopheline larvae were collected in standing water from several districts in Yaoundé, Cameroon (Tsinga, Nsam, Nkolbisson, Obobogo, Mvog-beti, Bastos, Tam-Tam, Nkoldongo) between September 2018 and September 2019 (Page 3, 'Study site').

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article investigating the fitness cost of insecticide resistance in Anopheles coluzzii.

sub_country_location.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from specific districts in Yaoundé, Cameroon (3° 52' 12 N; 11° 31' 12 E) (Page 3, 'Study site').

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Field collections took place from September 2018 to September 2019 (Page 3, 'Study site').

duplicate_risk.evidence: Primary field collections conducted specifically for this study in Yaoundé between 2018 and 2019.

supplement.evidence: All main genotype frequencies, counts, and bioassay data are reported in the main text and tables (e.g. Table 3).

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the fitness costs of insecticide resistance in Anopheles coluzzii from Yaoundé, Cameroon. Field-collected F0 larvae (92.5% An. coluzzii, 7.5% An. gambiae) were screened for kdr Vgsc 1014F and 1014S mutations, showing an F0 L1014F allele frequency of 58% (N=119: 24 RR, 90 RS, 5 SS). The selection of a resistant line over 12 generations resulted in 100% L1014F fixed frequency.
